youtube.baslik: Can a temporary threshold shift leave permanent damage? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In 2009, Kujawa and Liberman exposed mice to an eight to sixteen kilohertz noise at 100 decibels for two hours. Thresholds returned to normal in about two weeks and the outer hair cells remained intact; yet in parts of the cochlea, close to half of the inner hair cell synapses were permanently lost. There is direct histological evidence in humans for age-related synaptopathy; for noise-induced synaptopathy, the evidence is more indirect, and there is no validated clinical test.
